messages:
From: Linda Foster <audits@brightline.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Request: remediation timelines & scan artifact retention for SIG

Hi Neha,

As part of Brightline's SIG intake for vendors in our Q4 audit window, we need a short, confirmable statement of Redwood's typical CVE remediation windows by severity (we use CVSS semantics), plus how long you retain scan artifacts and raw findings (raw scanner output, patch evidence, ticket links) for third-party review.

Specific asks: 
- Typical SLAs: Critical (CVE-9+), High (7-8.9), Medium and Low (6.9 and below).
- Scan cadence for infra and app stacks (monthly/quarterly, on-demand after major deploy).
- Retention period for raw scan artifacts and where those artifacts are archived.
- Whether you can provide a signed attestation for a given quarter stating you met the SLA for affected CVEs and that artifacts will be made available on request.

We're hoping to get the info and an attestation placeholder by the end of next week. If you need to loop in engineering or security, please do so.

Thanks,
Linda Foster
Lead Vendor Assurance
Brightline Security

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Foster <audits@brightline.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-21T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: remediation timelines & scan artifact retention for SIG

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kim (Security Ops) and Ben (Customer Success / SOC2 owner) to confirm operational windows and archival process.

Prelim answers below so Brightline can progress the SIG intake: 

- SLAs (standard practice):
  • Critical (CVSS 9.0–10.0): 72 hours to initial remediation plan + 14 days to mitigation/patch where possible.
  • High (7.0–8.9): 7 calendar days for triage + 30 days target for remediation or documented compensating control.
  • Medium (4.0–6.9): 30–90 days depending on risk tier and exposure.
  • Low (<4.0): monitored; remediation typically scheduled in next regular maintenance window (90+ days).

- Scan cadence:
  • Infrastructure (internal infra + managed clusters): weekly authenticated scans + nightly dependency checks.
  • Application stacks (service images, infra-as-code): monthly app vulnerability scans and per-release SCA (software composition analysis).
  • On-demand scans are run after any major release or when a high/critical advisory is published.

- Artifact retention:
  • Raw scan outputs and triage logs retained for 1 year by default in our encrypted artifact store.
  • Triage tickets and remediation proof (patch links, CVE comments, PRs) retained for 3 years in our ticketing archive.
  • For longer retention or export for audits, we can package a time-bound handback (pdf/csv/zip) and deliver via a secure Drive link.

I've attached a concise CSV that summarizes our scan rhythm and a roster showing internal owners for remediation by component — see scan-rhythm-summary.csv and cve-ownership-roster.pdf.

Can Kim or Ben confirm the SLA language above and sign off on a one-quarter attestation template we can issue to Brightline?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

2) Could you provide a short, signed quarterly attestation PDF that states Redwood met its remediation SLAs for the July–September 2026 quarter and that artifacts will be available upon request for 12 months?

If you can get back with a signed attestation and a preferred delivery mechanism (Drive link v DocuSign) by the 27th, we can close Brightline's intake this week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Linda

Linda / Neha / Ben — following our internal review, confirming the SLA language and providing the requested attestation for Q3 2026. See summary and attached attestation PDF.

Short answers to Linda's clarifications: 
- The 14-day mitigation window for Critical CVEs includes documented temporary mitigations (network ACLs, firewall rules, config toggles, or similar compensating controls) if a code patch cannot be delivered within that window. All mitigations must be documented in the remediation ticket and linked to the CVE.
- We can provide the attestation as a signed PDF and deliver via a secure Drive link; for legal execution (if required) we can also route via DocuSign.

Attestation (summary): 
Redwood Inference certifies that for the period July 1, 2026 — September 30, 2026, vulnerability remediation activities were performed in accordance with the remediation cadence and SLAs documented in our security operations procedures. Relevant raw scan artifacts and remediation evidence will be retained for 12 months and made available to authorized auditors under NDA.

If Brightline needs a slightly different retention window or an expanded artifact set for compliance purposes, let us know and we will produce an export and tailored attestation.

Regards,

Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference
